name: Jude: Contending for the Faith
path: New Testament Studies: Life and Doctrine in Christ

objectives.text: Identify Jude as the writer of a short New Testament letter who called himself a servant of Jesus Christ and a brother of James
Recall from Jude's closing words that God is able to keep his people from stumbling
Recite the doxology of Jude from memory and name the things it gives to God
Identify the three words Jude uses to describe believers in his greeting as called, beloved, and kept
Explain in their own words what Jude means by urging believers to contend for the faith that was once for all delivered to the saints
Describe how Jude says false teachers crept into the church unnoticed and what two errors he says they taught
Retell the three Old Testament examples of judgment Jude uses and explain what each one warns about
Compare the way of Cain, the error of Balaam, and the rebellion of Korah using their Old Testament accounts
Explain the meaning of Jude's word pictures of hidden reefs, waterless clouds, fruitless trees, wild waves, and wandering stars
Contrast the restraint of the archangel Michael with the slander of the false teachers in Jude
Analyze how Jude quotes a prophecy attributed to Enoch and explain why the Reformed tradition holds that quoting a book does not make that book part of the canon
Explain the four commands Jude gives for believers to build themselves up, pray in the Holy Spirit, keep themselves in God's love, and wait for Christ's mercy
Explain how Jude uses the apostles' earlier predictions of scoffers to show that false teaching in the church was expected
Describe the different responses Jude commands toward those who doubt, those who must be snatched from the fire, and those to be shown mercy with fear
Construct a profile of the false teachers in Jude from the traits the letter assigns to them in belief, conduct, and speech
Evaluate the claim that grace permits sinful living by comparing Jude's warning with Paul's teaching and the Reformed confessions
Defend from Jude 1:3 and related texts the Reformed teaching that the faith was delivered once for all and is not added to by new revelations
Develop a plan for answering a false teaching that follows Jude's pattern of holding firm to truth while showing mercy to those who doubt
Synthesize Jude's warnings of judgment with his repeated theme of God keeping his people and explain how the tradition's doctrine of perseverance draws on the letter

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (authorship, God's keeping, contend for the faith, false teachers creeping in, Cain/Balaam/Korah, doxology, use of Enoch, building up in faith, mercy to doubters, apostate profile, grace into license, once-for-all faith, judgment and preservation). Dropped vague filler ('Name the fight for the truth', 'Observe warnings about bad leaders') and folded the Sodom item into a fuller objective on all three Old Testament judgment examples. Added missing content from Jude: the called/beloved/kept greeting, the metaphors of verses 12-13, Michael's restraint, the apostles' predicted scoffers, and an applied plan for answering error with mercy. Anchored each to specific verses and added confession references only where they state the doctrine (canon, sufficiency, grace and holiness, perseverance, prayer).
